title: Autumn Audio
statementMd:
![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/f7c3ccfe3e0eeb4bdb91ee206293d10cec5116e1.png)Image by Albert Bridge, from commons.wikimedia.org

As autumn approaches, amazing audio appears. Few things are as satisfying as the crunch of a dry leaf underfoot, except the crunch of a leaf under a bicycle, which comes twice: once from the front wheel, and once from the back.

You are walking through Reykjavík, listening to a single e-bike crunch its way down an otherwise empty street. In Iceland, e-bikes ride at exactly 1010 metres per second, the fastest speed at which the police still pretend not to notice. So the bike covers exactly one centimetre every millisecond. You wonder whether the crunches alone reveal the bike's wheelbase: the distance between the points where its two wheels touch the ground (or, equivalently, between the centres of its wheels).

You hear every crunch, and every leaf is crunched exactly twice: first by the front wheel, and later by the back wheel. You keep an open mind about the bike's dimensions: even a wheelbase of one centimetre or of a hundred kilometres is fine by you.

For example, suppose you hear 44 crunches, at milliseconds 100100, 200200, 300300 and 400400. There are two possible wheelbases.

The first possibility is that the wheelbase is 100100 centimetres and the two leaves are 200200 centimetres apart. Then the front wheel crunches the first leaf at 100100 and the back wheel crunches it at 200200; the front wheel crunches the second leaf at 300300 and the back wheel crunches it at 400400.

The second possibility is that the wheelbase is 200200 centimetres and the two leaves are 100100 centimetres apart. Then the front wheel crunches the first leaf at 100100 and the second leaf at 200200; the back wheel crunches the first leaf at 300300 and the second leaf at 400400.

## Input

The input consists of:

- One line with an even integer 𝑛n (2≤𝑛≤100002≤n≤10000), the number of crunches.
- One line with 𝑛n integers 𝑡1,…,𝑡𝑛t1,…,tn (1≤𝑡1≤⋯≤𝑡𝑛≤1091≤t1≤⋯≤tn≤109), the times of the crunches in milliseconds. Several crunches can happen at the same time; you hear each of them.

## Output

Output the number of possible wheelbases, followed by the possible wheelbases in centimetres, in increasing order, one per line. In particular, if no wheelbase is consistent with the crunches, output a single line with 00.
